**2026-10-29.** A patch release: a binary container for instance snapshots, two costs removed from
every completed instance, and a fix for local deliveries poisoned by a database restart. Everything
in the v0.6.0 release notes applies. Durability is unchanged — no commit was added or made
asynchronous; one separate transaction per completed instance became part of the instance's own
terminal commit. The database schema is unchanged (no migration); the `q:` namespace is untouched.

## Upgrade note — read before upgrading

0.6.7 writes instance snapshots in a binary container (format 5). It reads every snapshot an
earlier release wrote and rewrites one in format 5 the next time its instance commits.

**A release before 0.6.7 cannot read format 5.** It refuses such a row ("failed to decode persisted
instance snapshot: malformed \uXXXX encoding") and leaves the instance untouched. Therefore:

- **Upgrade the whole fleet at once**: stop every older replica, then start 0.6.7. Do not run 0.6.7
  next to an older replica on the same database.
- **Rolling back** to 0.6.6 or earlier works only for instances no 0.6.7 engine has committed.
  Finish or cancel the others first.

## Fixed

**A local delivery was poisoned when the database restarted under it.** A `local://` delivery whose
step failed because the database connection was reset, the pool timed out or the server was
shutting down got the generic `SUTRA.RUNTIME.UNEXPECTED` refusal and waited five minutes at the
poison horizon. Such failures are now marked `sutra.transient` and retried with the outbox backoff;
the step either did not commit or committed with its inbox dedup record, so the retry is processed
at most once. The PostgreSQL-crash conformance test failed on the 0.6.5 and 0.6.6 images in every
run here (one to three of 1500 orders not called back in time) and passes on 0.6.7.

## Changed

- **Snapshot format 5.** The same key/value map as before — keys, typed values, the
  `sutra.snapshot` generation, the encryption envelope and key id — stored as length-prefixed UTF-8
  behind the marker `\uSNAPSHOT/5\n` instead of escaped Properties text. Identical state still
  gives identical bytes; a malformed container is a decode error, never a partial instance. The
  conformance test `tc_snapshot_upgrade` parks instances on the published 0.6.5 and 0.6.6 images
  and resumes every one exactly once on 0.6.7. See *Durable execution: the binary container*.
- **The per-channel admission row is released inside the terminal commit**, for every instance,
  instead of in its own transaction afterwards.
- **Templates copy less**: the model converts the variables once, and is not deep-copied to strip
  null entries when it has none.

Measured in one session on one laptop with durable PostgreSQL:

| workload | 0.6.5 | 0.6.6 | 0.6.7 |
|---|---|---|---|
| relay, 500/s: CPU ms per completion (engine + PostgreSQL) | 10.43 | 8.25–8.35 | 7.91–8.06 |
| relay, 500/s: database transactions per completion | 13.9 | 14.2 | 13.1 |
| XML-heavy downstream workload, 400/s offered: completions/s (p99) | 300.4 (23.9 s) | 362.4 (9.7 s) | 400.0 (4.6 s) |
| the same, 500/s offered: completions/s | 286.6 | 315.3 | 335.8 |

## Install

```bash
docker pull ghcr.io/startr-trade/sutra:0.6.7
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/startr-trade/sutra/main/scripts/install.sh | sh -s -- --version v0.6.7
```

The library crates are on crates.io as `sutra-feel = "0.6.7"` and `sutra-dmn = "0.6.7"`.
